results.title: Ablakwa and the Evacuation of the Unborn
results.content: Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, our commitment to future generations became so impressive that we began evacuating citizens before they were born. Other countries were making plans for 2034 and 2036. We were already bringing their inhabitants home from South Africa. For years, politicians had been accused of doing nothing for the unborn. Here, at last, was documentary evidence that the unborn had benefited from foreign policy. Somewhere, a couple yet to meet could apparently rest assured that their future child had already escaped xenophobia.

results.title: Sand contractors seek regulatory clarity over enforcement operations at Dawa
results.content: The Sand and Stone Contractors Association of Ghana has called on state authorities to clarify the regulatory procedures governing sand-winning and transportation activities at Dawa and neighbouring communities. The Association says uncertainty surrounding enforcement operations, documentation requirements and the issuance of fines is creating difficulties for sand winners and tipper truck operators and requires urgent attention from the relevant institutions. In a petition signed by its Acting National Chairman, Anthony Mensah, the Association said it had approached several state institutions, including the Minerals Commission, the Ghana Military Police, the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ), the Tema Regional Police Command and the Member of Parliament for Ningo-Prampram, Samuel Nartey George, to seek intervention.
